title: What most money books agree on — and where they disagree
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Across Clason, Housel, Bogle, Sethi, Collins and others, a few points recur: pay yourself first and automate saving; live below your means; avoid expensive debt; build an emergency fund and protect against big risks; invest regularly in low-cost, diversified assets for the long term; and manage your own behaviour because emotions cost more than market moves. Real disagreements: Ramsey wants no credit cards and the debt snowball, while Sethi uses credit cards for rewards and favours optimising; Kiyosaki and Pabrai favour concentrated bets or leverage, whereas Bogle and Malkiel favour broad diversification; Buffett and Graham favour picking businesses, while Bogle says most people should not try; and Kiyosaki calls a home a liability, whereas many planners treat it as both housing and an asset. When books disagree, choose what fits your goals, risk and skills.
